NO CABIN YET
Week 9 · Writing Strong Opinions

Window or Aisle?

At check-in, the agent asks: "Window or aisle?" Nobody answers "Well, both have good points…". You choose, and you know why. DET opinion questions work the same way. This week you will pick a side, prove it with real reasons and examples, and hold your course when someone disagrees, just like the follow-up question in Interactive Writing. The four colours from Week 8 are back with new names. There's no grade, and finishing the steps counts as attending this week.

~25 min total Choose your level No sound needed One 5-minute opinion + a 3-minute follow-up
?Not sure what to do? Tap ? How it works at the top of any stop. You will see pictures and easy steps.
ChooseOne clear opinion: no fence, not extreme
ProveReal reasons, each with a specific example
Hold your courseAnswer the other side, then come back to yours
STOP 01~1 min

Choose Your Cabin

Pick the level that feels right today. Your choice changes the questions and how much you write. Every cabin counts the same for attendance, and you can switch any time.

STOP 02~3 min

Pre-flight Briefing

DET QUESTION · WRITING SAMPLE + INTERACTIVE WRITING

First, a quick question. On a plane, which seat do you choose?

Many DET writing questions ask for your opinion: the Writing Sample (30 seconds to plan, 5 minutes to write) and Interactive Writing (5 minutes, then a 3-minute follow-up question). A strong opinion paragraph uses the same four colours as last week:

OpinionYour side, said clearly in the first sentence.
ReasonAnswers the question "Why do you think that?"
ExampleProves the reason just before it with something real.
Final wordSays your opinion again to close the paragraph.

Now match each kind of sentence to its job: tap a name, then tap its job.

STOP 03~4 min

Pick a Seat

OPINION SKILL · A CLEAR SIDE

A strong first sentence picks a seat. Is each sentence a clear opinion, or does it make one of three mistakes? Tap your answer. Get them right in a row to build a streak 🔥.

SEATWHAT IT LOOKS LIKE
✓ Clear opinionOne side, said clearly: I think… / should… / is better than…
Sits on the fenceBoth sides, no choice: it depends, good and bad points
Just a factTrue information that nobody can disagree with
Too extremeToo strong to believe: everyone, never, the worst, completely
🔥 0
STOP 04~5 min

Passport & Customs

OPINION SKILL · REASONS AND EXAMPLES

At passport control, they ask "Why are you here?" At customs, they say "Show me." Your opinion needs both: a reason that answers why, and an example that shows it is true.

TIPA good example has a name, number, time or place: "last July in Osaka" proves more than "sometimes".

PART APassport control: which one is a real reason?

PART BCustoms: which example proves the reason?

STOP 05~4 min

Crosswind Landing

OPINION SKILL · ANSWERING THE OTHER SIDE

When a strong wind blows from the side, a pilot doesn't give up and doesn't ignore it. The pilot turns into the wind a little, then lands on the runway. When someone disagrees with you, do the same:

The crosswind landing

1. Agree a littleSay one small true thing about their idea.
It's true that… / That's a fair point. / Although… / Admittedly,…
→
2. Turn backCome back to your side with a reason.
However,… / But… / Yet… / Still,…

Three ways to crash: give in (change sides), ignore it (just repeat your opinion), or attack the person (be rude). In Interactive Writing, the 3-minute follow-up often asks about another side of your topic, so this skill is useful on test day.

STOP 06~10 min

Full Flight

DET PRACTICE · WRITING SAMPLE + INTERACTIVE WRITING FOLLOW-UP

Now choose your own seat. Read the question, 30 seconds to plan, then 5 minutes to write one opinion paragraph. Then, if you want, take the 3-minute crosswind follow-up, just like Interactive Writing. After that, colour your sentences and compare with a model.

STOP 07~2 min

Landing Card

This is Week 9's primary assignment. Check your Frequent Flyer Log, add one opinion-writing tip you will use on test day, then copy your summary and paste it into the Week 9 assignment in Classroom. That counts as attending this week.
